plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney DE + TF activity (Python)
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human kidney bulk RNA-seq samples (6 aldosterone-treated vs 6 vehicle, unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon gene counts, 12000 genes) with a single research question: which transcription factors drive the treated-vs-control response. The plan follows the DESeq2/pydeseq2-style workflow the knowledge service returned (grounded on the DE side): QC of sample structure, minimal low-count pre-filter, size-factor normalization inside the model, a Wald test with an explicit reference level (Vehicle) and contrast (Aldosterone vs Vehicle), apeglm shrinkage of the log2 fold change, BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05. The DE result (Wald statistic for every tested gene) then feeds two Python-only analyses that both answer the actual question: (1) decoupleR ulm TF-activity inference on the CollecTRI human regulon network (with DoRothEA A-C as a documented alternative, per the flagged small-cohort caveat that a self-inferred regulatory network from only 12 samples is not supportable — R-0121), and (2) fgsea-style preranked pathway enrichment (via gseapy prerank, since the user constraint is Python-only, not the R fgsea package) against MSigDB Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways-human sets, for mechanistic context around the TF hits. All steps use Python per the explicit user constraint; DESeq2/apeglm/decoupleR are invoked from Python through rpy2, since these are the grounded, validated implementations rather than untested Python reimplementations. The final report step ranks and names the top 6 TFs driving the response in each direction (activated / repressed) as the research question asks ("six per group"), states versions, thresholds, and the small-cohort caveats, and gives the fgsea/hallmark context beside the TF activity result. No translational (drug/safety/PK) scope was requested, so none is added.
